title: Pneumonia, Sputum Retention and Airway Clearance
lead: Not every patient with pneumonia needs chest physiotherapy. Learn who does.
case: Presentation (from the chapter): Sputum retention: Coarse crackles, weak or ineffective cough, rattly breathing, rising oxygen needs. Atelectasis: Reduced breath sounds at bases, dull percussion, low lung volumes after surgery or immobility. Increased work of breathing: High RR, accessory muscle use. Reduced mobility: Bed-bound, weak
working: Pneumonia, Sputum Retention and Airway Clearance
qa: Does airway clearance remove consolidation? No. Consolidation is inside the alveoli; airway clearance targets secretions in the airways.
What is the best single intervention for many pneumonia patients? Early mobilisation and upright positioning.
Describe a huff. A forced but open-glottis expiration, like fogging a mirror.
Name two contraindications to head-down drainage. Raised intracranial pressure and severe reflux or aspiration risk.
What sign suggests sputum retention? Coarse crackles with a weak, ineffective cough.

redFlags.Finding: Rising oxygen requirement, RR above about 30, confusion, falling BP
Desaturation during treatment not recovering with rest

manual.name: Positioning
manual.why: Upright sitting or side lying with the affected lung uppermost for drainage and ventilation

manual.name: Mobilisation
manual.why: Sit out of bed, stand, walk
manual.finding: Increases lung volumes and secretion movement

manual.name: Deep breathing with inspiratory hold
manual.why: 3 to 4 slow deep breaths, hold 2 to 3 s

manual.name: ACBT
manual.why: Breathing control, thoracic expansion exercises, forced expiration technique (huff)
manual.finding: Huff from mid-lung (medium breath, long huff) to high-lung (big breath, short huff)

manual.name: Modified postural drainage
manual.why: Position the affected segment so gravity helps drainage
manual.finding: Head-down tilt only if no contraindication

manual.name: Manual techniques (percussion, vibrations)
manual.why: Applied during expiration over the affected area
manual.finding: Adjunct; avoid over fractures, osteoporosis, low platelets

manual.name: Assisted cough
manual.why: Firm pressure under the ribs or wound support during cough

manual.name: Suction (nasopharyngeal or via airway)
manual.finding: When the patient cannot clear secretions

exerciseNotes: Progress from sitting out to walking, then to an exercise program before discharge if deconditioned. Older patients may need a structured rehabilitation pathway.
